ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC=4$, and $\angle B=\angle C=15^\circ$. What is the area of $\triangle ABC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw $CD \perp AB$ through point $C$ intersecting the extended line of $BA$ at $D$,\\
$\because$ $\angle B = \angle ACB = 15^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle CAD = \angle B + \angle ACB = 15^\circ + 15^\circ = 30^\circ$,\\
$\because$ $AC = 4$ and $CD$ is the height from the base $AB$,\\
$\therefore$ $CD = \frac{1}{2} AC = \frac{1}{2} \times 4 = 2$,\\
$\therefore$ the area of $\triangle ABC = \frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 2 = \boxed{4}$
